relations.note: Manco and Mama Ocllo are presented as children of the Sun.

relations.myth: The Sun gives the founders a golden rod
relations.note: The Sun gives Manco and Mama Ocllo a rod locating Cusco.

relations.myth: Manco prays before founding Cusco and Coricancha
relations.note: Manco prays to the Sun and establishes solar worship at Cusco.
relations.source: Cieza, El señorío de los incas

relations.note: Garcilaso presents Mama Ocllo as Manco's sister.
Mama Ocllo is Manco's wife in the dominant solar-couple tradition.

relations.myth: Solar couple travels from Titicaca and founds Cusco
relations.note: She co-founds Cusco, gathers women, and teaches household and textile work.
Some Ayar configurations place Mama Huaco among Manco's sisters.
relations.source: Betanzos, Suma y narración de los incas

relations.note: Variant Ayar pairings make Mama Huaco Manco's wife.
Guaman Poma makes Mama Huaco Manco's mother or origin-source.

relations.myth: Mama Huaco helps seize the Cusco valley
relations.note: She defeats or terrifies the Huallas and helps Manco's migrants seize Cusco.
Ayar Cachi is one of Ayar Manco's three brothers.
relations.source: Betanzos, Suma y narración de los incas

relations.myth: Ayar Cachi is trapped inside the origin cave
relations.note: Manco participates in or benefits from deceiving and enclosing his dangerous brother.
Ayar Uchu is Manco's brother and becomes the Huanacauri huaca.

relations.myth: Ayar Uchu becomes Huanacauri and guides Manco
relations.note: After transformation, Ayar Uchu instructs Manco and promises continued assistance.
relations.source: Betanzos, Suma y narración de los incas

relations.myth: Manco petitions the brother-huaca before founding Cusco
relations.note: Manco prays to Huanacauri for favor and reveres him as a god.
relations.source: Cieza, El señorío de los incas

relations.note: Ayar Auca is one of Ayar Manco's three brothers.
relations.source: Betanzos, Suma y narración de los incas

relations.myth: Ayar Auca supernaturally takes possession of Cusco
relations.note: Manco directs or accompanies Auca, then inherits the political result of his land-taking.

relations.myth: Creator moves the ancestors underground toward Pacaritambo
relations.note: A late variant makes the Creator bring Manco's ancestral group from Titicaca.

relations.myth: Manco founds Cusco invoking Ticci Viracocha
relations.note: Manco founds Cusco in the name of Ticci Viracocha and other gods.
relations.source: Cieza, El señorío de los incas

relations.note: Sinchi Roca is usually Manco's son and dynastic successor.

relations.myth: Theosophical comparison of Andean and Egyptian divine couples
relations.note: Blavatsky compares Manco with Osiris in an occult diffusionist scheme.

relations.myth: Theosophists classify Manco among universal divine kings
relations.note: Later Theosophical writers compare Manco with Manu as a divine instructor.

relations.myth: Theosophists classify Manco among universal divine kings
relations.note: Later Theosophical writers compare Manco with Hermes as a civilizing divine king.

relations.myth: Theosophists compare legendary founders across civilizations
relations.note: Later Theosophical writing compares Manco with Menes as a primordial founder.
